content: Figure FIGREF19 shows the architecture of our DNN algorithm. Every input word had an associated list of $n$ features, and we trained randomly initialized embeddings of size 100 for each feature. Then, we concatenated the feature embeddings vectors creating an $n\times 100$ vector for each word. We fed these vectors into a biLSTM layer of 100 dimensions after applying a dropout of 75%, where dropout behaves like a regularlizer to avoid overfitting BIBREF40. We conducted side experiments with lower dropout rates, but the higher dropout rate worked best. The output of the biLSTM layer was fed into a 100 dimensional dense layer with 15% dropout and softmax activation. We conducted side experiments where we added additional biLSTM layers and replaced softmax with a conditional random field layer, but we did not observe improvements. Thus, we opted for a simpler model. We used a validation set to determine optimal parameters such as dropout rate. Again, we used the “Adamax” optimizer with categorical cross entropy loss and a learning rate of 0.001. We also applied early stopping with patience of up to 5 consecutive epochs without improvement.
